Step 1:  Translate the given abundance ratios into [Si/H] for each star.

Star 1  
[Si/Fe]₁ = [Si/H]₁ – [Fe/H]₁  
0.3 dex   = [Si/H]₁ – 0 dex  
⇒ [Si/H]₁ = +0.3 dex

Star 2  
[Mg/Si]₂ = [Mg/H]₂ – [Si/H]₂  
0.3 dex   = 0 dex – [Si/H]₂  
⇒ [Si/H]₂ = –0.3 dex

Step 2:  Convert [Si/H] to number ratios relative to the Sun.

Star 1:  nSi₁ / nSi⊙ = 10^{+0.3} ≈ 1.995  
Star 2:  nSi₂ / nSi⊙ = 10^{–0.3} ≈ 0.501

Step 3:  Take the ratio of silicon atoms between the two stars.

(nSi₁ / nSi⊙) ÷ (nSi₂ / nSi⊙) = 10^{0.3 – (–0.3)} = 10^{0.6} ≈ 3.98 ≈ 3.9

Hence the ratio of silicon atoms in the photospheres of Star 1 to Star 2 is about 3.9.

Answer: D
